name: Walangama
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.note: Lists Black 1980 as the only comment (on subclassification); status extinct; no descriptive references (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).
Nothing; 'poorly attested', AIATSIS code G36, cites AUSTLANG and Bowern 2011 blog list only.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Change Request 2012-111: create [nlw] Walangama (submitted by A. Aristar, MultiTree, supported by C. Bowern; adopted 2013-01-23). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing. Justifies the code with AIATSIS/AUSTLANG listing and Black 2004: 253 ('Walangama, in the Croyden area, is an initial dropping language..'); other sources are Tindale 1974, Walsh 1981, AusAnthrop, Bowern p.c.

sources.citation: Black, Paul D. 1980. Norman Pama historical phonology. In B. Rigsby & P. Sutton (eds), Papers in Australian Linguistics No. 13 (Pacific Linguistics A-59), 181-239. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Section 9 'Walangama phonological developments' (pp. 216-218) says nothing about stress: Walangama is 'extinct but also almost completely unknown to contemporary informants', known from up to 300 words in Palmer 1884, Curr 1886, Dutton 1904 and Tindale 1938, and 'the transcriptions tend to be too imprecise to permit a detailed comparison'. Stress statements exist only for Kurtjar (p. 196: predictably on the first syllable of a word), Kuthant (p. 197: non-contrastive, first long vowel else first vowel), Koko-Bera/Kok-Nar (p. 198: contrastive) and Kukatj (not transcribed). No 'stress'/'accent'…

sources.citation: Armit, William E. 1886. No. 93. Middle Norman [Wollongurmee tribe]. In Edward M. Curr, The Australian Race, vol. 2, 310-313. Melbourne: John Ferres.
sources.note: Nothing. A ~120-item wordlist plus nine phrases in Curr's lay orthography with no accent marks; Curr's only comment is that the language 'differs so much from its neighbours' and that he has been 'particularly careful' with the pronoun forms. No pronunciation remark.

sources.citation: Palmer, Edward. 1884. Notes on some Australian tribes. Journal of the Anthropological Institute of Great Britain and Ireland 13: 276-347 (Appendix I, vocabulary of Aboriginal words, pp. 326-334).
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix I is a multi-column comparative wordlist (Burnett, Saxby/Mycoolon, Mitchell/Koogominny, Gilbert River, Myappe, etc.) with no accent marks and no remark on stress or pronunciation; the only 'accent' hits in the volume belong to other papers.

sources.citation: Black, Paul. 2004. The failure of the evidence of shared innovations in Cape York Peninsula. In C. Bowern & H. Koch (eds), Australian Languages: Classification and the Comparative Method, 241-268. Amsterdam: Benjamins.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Later classification paper; p. 253 calls Walangama an initial-dropping language (per ISO CR 2012-111). Could contain a passing remark on Norman Pama stress but is not a description.

sources.citation: Black, Paul. 1976b. Walangama. Unpublished manuscript (cited in Black 1980: 'Black (1976b) is currently attempting to collate and analyse all known Walangama data'); probably deposited with AIATSIS.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only dedicated analysis of Walangama phonology ever. if any statement about stress exists it would be here, though its base is the same unaccented wordlists so a stress rule is unlikely.

sources.citation: Sutton, Peter. 1976. The diversity of initial dropping languages in southern Cape York. In P. Sutton (ed.), Languages of Cape York, 102-123. Canberra: AIAS.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, full text not open (only the abstract or a snippet is); only the abstract or an excerpt is openly accessible
sources.note: Survey of initial-dropping languages (initial dropping in this region is usually tied to stress shift); may mention Walangama and stress-conditioned changes, but is an overview, not a description.

sources.citation: Black, Paul. 1975, 1977. [Reports to A.I.A.S. on Normanton research, 1974-7]. Unpublished manuscript, AIATSIS MS 462, 4 parts (notes on phonology, morphology and syntax of Kurtjar, Kuthant, Kukatj, Rib, Walangama, Kok-Nar).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Black's field reports include Walangama among the languages treated; may hold his collation of the old Walangama data and any rememberer forms.

sources.citation: Tindale, Norman B. 1938. Unpublished Walangama vocabulary (Harvard-Adelaide expedition field notes; cited in Black 1980: 187).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Last first-hand attestation of the language; Tindale's vocabularies sometimes mark stress with an acute, so this is the only conceivable source of any accent information for Walangama.

sources.citation: Dutton, [?]. 1904. Wordlists ('Bourke District' etc.), pp. 24-26 (Walangama data pp. 25-26, as cited in Black 1980: 187).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: One of the four Walangama attestation sources; wordlist only, would not state stress.
